title: The 10am NQ setup only made money in uptrends, and holding the Nasdaq beat it by about 74 points over the same window
author: person-person12
selftext:
Most ppl checking a strategy look at whether it made money. The question that matters more is whether it made money in a way that just holding the index wouldnt have done better.

I rebuilt the 10am NQ setup that was all over my feed, where you mark the 10am candle, wait for one side to get swept and take the move back through, and ran it in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) on 1m NQ candles from july 2023 to feb 2026, 1 contract on a 100k account. 535 trades, 60.2% wins, profit factor 0.98, **net -$3,675**.

Then I split the trades by what the market was doing when each one was taken. **280 of the 535 came in volatile conditions and lost $6,764** at a 0.93 profit factor. The only stretch where it made money was uptrends, 152 trades at a 1.08 profit factor for +$3,307.

So the part of the curve that looked like an edge was mostly the Nasdaq going up, and holding the Nasdaq over the same window took 100k to about 170k while the setup finished at -3.7%.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: Splitting by regime is the part most people skip. 60% wins with a 0.98 profit factor also means the losers were bigger than the winners, so I'm curious how much of that -$3,675 is just commissions and slippage over 535 trades.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: The bigger piece is the shape, not the costs. The average loss was $806 against a $522 average win, because you get filled on the close back through the 10am level but the stop is measured off the level itself, so by the time youre in the stop is **already further away than the target**. At 60% wins it needed the winners to be about 0.67x the losers and it came in at 0.65.

replies.author: AoideusWasBanned
replies.body: Ah, that makes sense. So the fill already puts you behind on the stop distance before the trade even starts. 0.65 vs the 0.67 it needed is painfully close too. Did you try measuring the stop from the actual fill instead of the level?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: this is your SPY dip post from October in a different coat: there two years carried the total, here the uptrend slice does. 152 trades at 1.08 while the index went up 70% is long beta with more steps. were commissions already inside the 0.98, or does it get worse?

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Fair comparison tbh, both times one stretch carried the whole total and the rest gave it back. **Long beta with more steps** is a pretty good way to put it, the uptrend slice is the only one that made money and its also the slice where just holding the index did better.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: then the test left is the boring one: inside that uptrend slice, hold NQ only for the minutes the setup is in a trade and compare. if the setup can't beat that, the 10am rule adds nothing and the trend filter was the whole strategy. useful result either way, most people never slice it at all.

comments.author: Substantial_Air_3170
comments.body: The 0.98 profit factor across 535 trades says much more than the 60.2% win rate. If the only profitable stretch was an uptrend where simply holding Nasdaq did better, the setup probably isn't adding much edge. That's something I keep in mind on moon too. Being directionally correct isn't the same as outperforming a simpler approach.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Yea thats exactly it. The 152 uptrend trades made **+$3,307 at a 1.08 profit factor**, and holding the Nasdaq over the same window took 100k to about 170k, so being right on direction was never the hard part. It needed one regime where it beat doing nothing and it didnt have one.
